creditDraft: James Sharples, National Portrait Gallery, Smithsonian · public domain
altDraft: Pastel portrait of a man with grey hair, dark coat and white neckcloth, looking toward the viewer against a blue-grey background.
concerns: Drawn in America (Sharples was in the US from 1796) when Priestley was about 64, so it is not 'England' or the 1770s of the story. Rights proof taken from the Commons page; the Smithsonian page did not render its rights line for curl, so open-access status there is unchecked (not needed, the age proof covers it). Identity is the museum's own title and well attested. Tall 3:4 portrait; large file (10 MB), downsize before shipping.

creator: Joseph Priestley (author); plate signed 'Butterworth sc. Leeds' (engraver)

storyLink: Anchor 'story (given, not a business)': he published a way anyone could make it (P F12, 1772 pamphlet); also the fizzy water of paragraph 0.
pdReasonUS: Taken from the pamphlet itself, published London 1772; Wellcome Public Domain Mark; Commons 'Public domain'.
pdReasonUKEU: Priestley died 1804 and the engraver's work is anonymous and over 240 years old.
altDraft: Engraved plate of a glass jar standing in a bowl of water, with tubes, a bladder and a bottle, labelled Fig. 1 to 3.
concerns: Resolution is only 880x1552 (long side ok, width below 1000). Shows his glass-and-bladder method, not the brewery vat of paragraph 0 (the plate is the 'copyable way' of paragraph 1). Foxing and paper show-through are genuine. Wellcome's own page is the highest-resolution source offered; I did not look for a larger scan.
